title: CAMIMEX Sets 40% Emissions Cut with TSM Standard - Mexico Business News
content: CAMIMEX has committed to reducing Mexico's mining sector GHG emissions by 40% by 2030 through the adoption of the TSM standard, a Canadian framework requiring facility-level reporting and third-party audits every three years. The target spans 97 open-pit mines and 152 underground operations, with renewable energy use set to rise from 36% to 44%, responding to mounting pressure from institutional investors demanding verifiable ESG benchmarks. The initiative directly affects major operators in Sonora and Zacatecas and aligns with the Mexico–Canada Action Plan 2025–2028 and North American critical mineral supply chain priorities. CAMIMEX has announced a commitment to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from Mexico's mining sector by 40% before the end of the decade, backed by the formal adoption of the Towards Sustainable Mining (TSM) standard developed by the Mining Association of Canada (MAC). The initiative represents the most concrete, verifiable decarbonization target the sector has established to date, and positions Mexico as a key player in North America's shift toward responsible mineral extraction. The move comes as institutional investors and international markets have intensified demands for auditable environmental indicators, and as the mining industry seeks to reinforce Mexico's standing as a destination for foreign capital tied to the energy transition. Unlike many ESG frameworks that rely on voluntary disclosures, TSM requires facility-level reporting and external audits every three years. The standard, originally launched in 2004, is structured around three pillars: Communities and People, Environmental Stewardship, and Energy Efficiency. Each pillar includes performance indicators that companies must measure and disclose publicly. The framework also mandates the creation of Community Advisory Panels composed of representatives from Indigenous groups, local communities, NGOs and labor organizations, designed to support dialogue, identify emerging risks and promote accountability through direct engagement between companies and stakeholders. With its adoption of the TSM standard, Camimex became the 11th mining association in the world and the fifth in Latin America to join the framework. The licensing agreement was first signed in March 2023 at the annual convention of the Association of Prospectors & Developers of Canada, and has since been deepened through binational cooperation. In October 2025, members of the Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Mexico's (CANCHAM) Mining Executive Committee formally committed to implementing the standard across all operational stages, including exploration, production and mine closure. The decarbonization commitment spans the full breadth of Mexico's extractive sector. Implementation will cover the 97 open-pit mines and 152 underground operations that make up the national mining industry, a scale that makes the verification requirements of the TSM standard particularly significant. On the energy side, 41 mining units currently generate or consume renewable energy, accounting for 36% of total industry energy use. CAMIMEX members aim to raise that share to 44% by 2030, in line with Mexico's climate goals and global mining benchmarks. Pedro Rivero, President, CAMIMEX, noted in the 2025 Sustainability Report that the industry has strengthened its environmental commitment through increased investments in sustainability and the adoption of technologies that optimize water and energy use, reduce emissions, and help prevent, mitigate, offset, and restore the impacts resulting from its operations. Water management has also emerged as a key metric. In 2024, mining used only 0.27% of all water concessions in Mexico, with 70–71% of its water supply coming from recirculated sources, including closed-loop systems and treated wastewater. These results were made possible through continuous investment in water treatment, with the sector now operating 100 treatment plants nationwide. The targets will face their most demanding test in Mexico's two dominant mining states. Sonora, which contributes 45% of national production value, hosts large-scale operations such as Grupo México's Buenavista del Cobre, which has faced scrutiny over historical water conflicts. Zacatecas, home to major transnational operators including Newmont's Peñasquito and Fresnillo PLC, will require aligning the TSM framework with existing corporate sustainability commitments already established at a global level. Fernando Aboitiz, Head, Extractive Activities Coordination Unit at Mexico's Ministry of Economy, said the government views mining development through the lens of high social and environmental standards, describing collaboration between CAMIMEX and CANCHAM as a necessary step to strengthen sustainability, particularly as North America seeks to secure supply chains for critical minerals tied to the energy transition. The industry is also expanding investment in copper, silver, zinc, fluorspar, and graphite, minerals essential for solar technologies, electric vehicle batteries, hydrogen systems, and next-generation electronics. CAMIMEX has framed the TSM adoption as a strategic response to evolving financial market conditions, not only a regulatory or reputational measure. Institutional investors have increasingly required verifiable environmental benchmarks before committing capital to mining projects or purchasing sustainable bonds. Many mining companies worldwide, including Mexican companies, have committed to ambitious sustainability goals, ranging from carbon neutrality by 2040 to reducing operational emissions by 30% by 2030. Others pledge to concentrate on Scope 1 and 2 emissions reductions by 2030 and net zero by 2050. CAMIMEX's 40% reduction target, backed by third-party verification, places the Mexican sector among the more ambitious commitments in the Latin American region. The broader industry context underscores the urgency. Globally, the mining and metals sector accounts for approximately 4% to 7% of greenhouse gas emissions. In countries like Chile, copper mining alone contributes 30% of national emissions. Mexico has sought to avoid a similar concentration of environmental liability as its extractive sector grows. Karen Flores, Director General, CAMIMEX, emphasized the timing of the initiative, pointing to the alignment with the Mexico–Canada Action Plan 2025–2028 and North American ESG requirements as central drivers. According to Rivero, the TSM standard will reinforce the sector's technical credibility and help maintain Mexico's competitiveness as a mining investment destination. With external audits, public reporting requirements and community oversight panels built into the framework, the 2030 commitment marks a structural shift in how Mexico's mining industry intends to account for its environmental footprint and in how it will be judged by the markets that fund it. © 2025 Mexicobusiness.News. title: Monsoon Season In Southeastern Arizona: Preparing For Summer Storms And Power Outages - allhitskzmk.com

title: TSM Stock Slips Premarket Today — CEO Reportedly Says AI Chip Shortage Isn’t Ending Anytime Soon - Stocktwits
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) CEO C.C. Wei reportedly told shareholders at the annual meeting in Taiwan that AI chip demand will outpace supply for years to come, even as one of the world's biggest chipmakers races to expand its manufacturing footprint. Wei's commentary hinted that production capacity is one of the bottlenecks at a time when hyperscalers and chip companies are investing heavily to build AI infrastructure. According to a Bloomberg report, Wei said the company will not be able to meet demand from its American customers even after its manufacturing facilities become operational in the U.S. At the time of writing, TSM stock was down over 2% premarket on Thursday. In an earnings call post the Q1 announcement, company management stated that it had acquired two land parcels in Arizona to build additional fabs and meet multiyear demand from its U.S. customers. Later in April, according to a Reuters report, the company management said that it plans to open a chip packaging facility by 2029. Despite the supply-demand gap, Wei added that TSMC will refrain from suddenly increasing prices to maintain a stable business, the report stated. However, Wei reportedly added that it will be a long time before the company can meet customer demand. Major hyperscalers are set to spend billions on AI infrastructure this year alone, and TSMC produces the majority of the world's advanced AI chips. As a part of the U.S.-Taiwan trade pact, TSMC envisions building at least four more US chipmaking plants on top of six already planned, a total of 10 facilities entailing $165 billion in announced investments plus roughly $100 billion in additional capital, according to the report. Two plots of land acquired in Arizona should be enough to satisfy TSMC's needs for a decade, Wei said. The expansion is critical as TSMC is essential for Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, AMD's MI450/Helios chips, and custom ASICs from Broadcom and others. The company raised its full-year sales guidance in April and said capital spending should trend toward the upper end of its $56 billion forecast range. Shares of CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (CRWD) were on track for the worst single-day fall in 22 months in Thursday’s pre-market session after its first-quarter (Q1) results disappointed investors. CrowdStrike reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.1 on revenue of $1.39 billion, compared to Wall Street estimates of an EPS of $1.07 on revenue of $1.36 billion, according to Fiscal.ai data. However, analysts at Jefferies noted that while CrowdStrike’s annual recurring revenue growth of $6 million beat the consensus estimates, the beat was not large enough, according to TheFly. CrowdStrike shares were down more than 11% during Thursday’s pre-market trade. CRWD was among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. However, CrowdStrike's $6 million ARR beat versus consensus fell well short of the $15 million to $29 million upside delivered in each of the previous four quarters, the firm said. According to Jefferies, the smaller-than-usual ARR beat, combined with elevated investor expectations following the stock's 97% rally since April 10, weighed on shares after earnings. Barclays analyst Saket Kalia raised his price target on CrowdStrike to $675 from $650 while maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating. Kalia noted that net new annual recurring revenue rose to $256 million but fell short of its upside scenario, as deals generated from the Mythos launch in April are expected to take longer to close. The firm stated that investors appear to be pushing back on the size of CrowdStrike's Q1 beat. Analysts at TD Cowen stated that investors were looking for a larger upside surprise after the stock surged roughly 40% over the past month. The firm raised its price target on CrowdStrike to $700 from $625, reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating, and added that the post-earnings sell-off should prove transitory. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz stated that the company’s record net new ARR, QuiltWorks coalition, and AIDR innovation are indicators of its own AI inflection point. “We're seeing platform adoption from existing customers, new logo lands, and increased partner engagement, each giving me the conviction to significantly raise our FY27 net new ARR guidance. The technology is here. The team is here. And the market opportunity is ours,” Kurtz said. Shares of Rivian Automotive, Inc. (RIVN) slid 1% overnight heading into Wednesday after the EV maker officially opened R2 ordering and began public customer deliveries, with early buyers raising concerns over lease costs, financing terms and software features missing at launch. RIVN stock slumped 7% on Tuesday, with shares on a downward trend after logging a record streak last week in anticipation of the R2 launch. Rivian opened R2 orders on Tuesday and began customer deliveries of the midsize SUV, which is key to the EV maker's plans to broaden its customer base and hit profitability. The company also revealed the first lease and financing terms for R2. A 36-month lease on the R2 Performance AWD is estimated at $829 per month with $3,500 down, while a 24-month lease rises to $949. With lower down payments, monthly costs can exceed $1,000. Lease analyst Travis Ketchum calculated an all-in payment of about $988 per month with zero down and estimated an effective lease APR of 9.62%. "With the launch of Rivian R2 'underway' as of this week, we finally have lease and finance numbers," Ketchum said on X. "As expected, the residual is solid but the money factor is... rough." His lease-rating model assigned the deal a score of 43 out of 100, classifying it as "poor." Buyers also drew comparisons with Tesla's Model Y, which currently carries financing offers as low as 0%-0.99% APR. Others questioned the R2's value proposition relative to Rivian's own lineup, noting that the larger R1S Dual Standard leases for around $899 per month and includes a $3,000 incentive despite carrying a significantly higher sticker price. Some prospective customers said that the narrow lease gap between the R2 and R1 made the smaller SUV a tougher sell, according to EV. Early attendees at Rivian's First Drive events also noted that several software features available on current R1 vehicles will not be available when the R2 launches. Among the missing features are Rivian Assistant, Climate Hold, Pet Mode, Google Casting, YouTube integration, SiriusXM and the Camp Mode application. Gear Guard will launch with limited functionality. Rivian has said that the features will arrive through future software updates, but has not provided firm timelines. When the company unveiled the R2 in March 2024, it promoted the SUV with a headline starting price of $45,000 and positioned it as the vehicle that would make the brand "accessible to so many more people." However, the first version available to order is the R2 Performance Launch Edition priced at $57,990. The Premium trim is expected later in 2026, while the Standard Long Range variant is scheduled for the first half of 2027. The long-awaited entry-level model carrying the promised $44,990-$45,000 price tag is not expected until summer 2027. Rivian is targeting 20,000 to 25,000 deliveries in 2026 as part of its overall guidance of 62,000 to 67,000 vehicles. With R1 and commercial van volumes expected to remain largely flat, much of Rivian's growth hinges on a successful R2 ramp. We will be range bound for forceable future if not then at least next 2 to 3 quarters.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Seabreeze Partners Management President Doug Kass stated on Tuesday that he values SpaceX at a nearly 50% discount to the offer price, days ahead of its Nasdaq debut later this week. Kass said in a post on X that his firm, Seabreeze Partners, concluded that SpaceX's intrinsic value is well below the proposed offer price. While acknowledging that the shares could initially trade above the offer price, Kass said his firm declined an invitation to participate in the IPO. “We currently plan to short the stock - but that could change subject to markets and price,” he added. According to Kass, Seabreeze Partners values SpaceX at roughly $70 per share, based on a range of potential business outcomes, representing a discount of about 48% to the offer price. SpaceX plans to raise $75 billion through its IPO, priced at $135 per share and valuing the company at roughly $1.75 trillion. Morningstar analysts stated in a note on Tuesday that they believe the SpaceX IPO is overvalued. The firm values the SpaceX IPO at $63 per share, which is a discount of about 53% to the offer price. Kass criticized the quality of commentary surrounding the IPO, saying many market pundits discussing SpaceX had not conducted rigorous valuation work. He specifically criticized financial television coverage of the IPO, arguing that commentators were speaking in "glittering generalities" while offering confident opinions on valuation. "Not one talking head said 'I don't know' when asked about the value of SpaceX," Kass wrote, adding that few had likely read the company’s registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Meanwhile, investment banks Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley released their revenue forecasts for SpaceX, expecting the company’s topline to soar over the coming years. Morgan Stanley expects SpaceX’s revenue to surge about 182-fold to $3.4 trillion by 2040, from $18.7 billion in 2025. Goldman Sachs, SpaceX’s lead investment bank, expects the Elon Musk-led aerospace giant’s revenue to rise to $474 billion by 2030, while it forecasts AI revenue to come in at $322 billion. Morgan Stanley stated in its note that SpaceX could post adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) of $2.7 trillion by 2040. Goldman expects SpaceX’s adjusted EBITDA to soar over 52-fold to $352 billion by 2030, from $6.6 billion in 2025. content: I said it earlier today when I was on the 1st Ave. stage at Thursdays Downtown introducing one of the bands...and I'll say it again...I LOVE this event in Rochester! If you've never gone to Thursdays Downtown - or maybe you just haven't had a chance to get there recently - find a Thursdays this summer and add this popular event in the Med City to your calendar.  It is one you do NOT want to miss this summer.  Below are a few of the top things you'll find at this event that brings thousands to the downtown area. READ MORE: Tinn's Brought Their Food Truck Back To Rochester - Here's Where You Can Find It If you are looking for a fun block-party-style event, Thursdays Downtown in Rochester is the place to be.  Just head to 1st Ave. on Thursdays from June 11th until August 13th this year for food, live music, and family-friendly fun. If you haven't had a chance to check it out for yourself, here's what you'll find once you head to the Peace Plaza and 1st Ave. area. There are a few booths that are set up that have people who are there to help answer all of your questions.  You can also grab a free Thursdays Downtown sticker. title: TSM Stock Hits New Record Above $460 as Nvidia Collab and Packaging Deals Drive Momentum - FXLeaders
content: Taiwan Semiconductor TSMC’s steady climb to record highs reflects powerful AI-driven demand, though rising geopolitical and capacity constraints continue to temper the outlook. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company extended its upward momentum on Thursday, briefly surpassing $460 to reach a new record high. The move reflects sustained investor confidence in the company’s central role in global semiconductor supply chains, particularly as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to accelerate. The rally has been supported by a series of strategic developments that reinforce TSMC’s long-term production visibility and technological leadership, even as broader semiconductor markets face cyclical uncertainty. A key driver of sentiment is TSMC’s newly announced ten-year collaboration with Amkor Technology. Under the agreement, TSMC will outsource advanced packaging and testing services in Arizona, expanding its U.S.-based manufacturing ecosystem. The partnership is designed to improve supply chain resilience while supporting TSMC’s ongoing expansion in the United States. It also provides clearer long-term visibility into packaging capacity, an increasingly critical component of advanced chip production for AI and high-performance computing workloads. Additional optimism stems from TSMC’s deepening cooperation with Nvidia. The two companies are working together to integrate AI tools into semiconductor manufacturing processes, including computational lithography, wafer inspection, and transistor-level simulation. By embedding advanced AI models into fabrication workflows, TSMC aims to improve production yields and shorten development cycles, reinforcing its technological edge at the leading edge of chip manufacturing. Customer demand for advanced nodes continues to be a central growth driver. Chips built on TSMC’s 3-nanometer process now account for roughly a quarter of total revenue, up sharply from just a few years ago, reflecting rapid adoption in AI and high-performance computing applications. Major customers, including Marvell Technology, are also exploring early adoption of next-generation process technologies, signaling a strong backlog of advanced-node demand extending well into the next decade. Despite the strong fundamentals, TSMC shares declined more than 3% following the announcement in April, but that was just a pullback before the uptrend resumed again. The stock reached a new record at $450 in early June, but retreated lower, however this week is another bullish one and the TSMC stock has printed a new record at $465 with the 20 weekly SMA (gray) acting as support during pullbacks. TSMC has reiterated a confident long-term outlook, projecting more than 30% revenue growth in U.S. dollar terms for 2026, supported by elevated capital expenditure plans. The company continues to expand manufacturing capacity across Taiwan, the United States, and Japan, including its $165 billion investment program in Arizona. However, management has acknowledged that semiconductor fab construction remains a multi-year process, with new capacity typically requiring two to three years to come online. Despite the strong outlook, management has highlighted geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East, as a potential near-term source of volatility. In addition, the pace of global AI demand is placing strain on existing capacity, raising the risk of supply bottlenecks during the expansion phase. Overall, while TSMC’s structural growth story remains firmly supported by AI-driven demand and long-term customer commitments, execution timelines and geopolitical uncertainty continue to shape a more cautious near-term outlook. TSMC’s results reinforce the strength of the chip cycle, but the muted stock reaction serves as a reminder that expectations are already high. Sustaining upside will depend not just on demand, but on execution, macro stability, and the company’s ability to translate growth into consistent returns.

title: Rochester’s Newest Splash Pad is Opening Soon - Quick Country 96.5
content: Have you spotted the brand-new splash pad on Marion Road? It looks totally finished, yet there’s not a kid in sight. If you’ve been wondering what the hold-up is, I have the inside scoop, and some great news. The wait for Rochester’s newest summer hot spot is almost over! According to a recent press release from the City of Rochester, McQuillan Splash Pad is basically done, but there is one last piece of standard red tape keeping it closed to the public. After wrapping up construction, the Minnesota Department of Health stepped in with a few extra water safety requirements. The good news is that the city is already working on installing those upgrades right now. Once that's all set and passes a final inspection, the water is officially getting turned on for the summer! The city didn't hold back on this build. It’s a massive 2,480-square-foot facility packed with 19 interactive water features. Zoned for All Ages: The layout is split into dedicated toddler, family, and teen bays. Built for Everyone: Accessibility was a major priority here. The pad includes two wheelchair-accessible activators and is surrounded by accessible sidewalks. Parent-Approved Amenities: They’ve included a new restroom facility, shade elements to hide from the midday sun, and plenty of benches/picnic tables for us to sit on while keeping an eye on the chaos. A tiny bit of that final work depends on Mother Nature cooperating, but city officials are highly optimistic that we’ll be splashing around for one of the busiest, hottest holiday weekends of the summer - that's right, 4th of July weekend! Once they are officially open for the season, McQuillan Splash Pad will be open daily from 10a-8p. It's absolutely free to go. If the kids are already bouncing off the walls and you can't wait until July, Rochester has a few other excellent spots worth checking out: Lincolnshire Park Splash Pad: Completely free to use and open daily.
